Our principal executive office is located at 701 Market Street, Suite 300, Philadelphia, PA 19106 and our telephone number is (215) 546-7909. Our corporate website address is www.fivebelow.com. The information contained on, or accessible through, our corporate website does not constitute part of this Annual Report. As used herein, “Five Below,” the “Company,” “we,” “us,” “our” or “our business” refers to Five Below, Inc. (collectively with its wholly owned subsidiaries), except as expressly indicated or unless the context otherwise requires. As used herein, references to “crew” refers to our employees, and references to “shipcenters” refers to our distribution and logistics centers. We purchase products in reaction to existing marketplace trends and, hence, refer to our products as “trend-right.” We use the term “dynamic” merchandise to refer to the broad range and frequently changing nature of the products we display in our stores. We use the term “power” shopping center to refer to an unenclosed shopping center with 250,000 to 750,000 square feet of gross leasable area that contains three or more “big box” retailers (large retailers with floor space over 50,000 square feet) and various smaller retailers with a common parking area shared by the retailers.

With most items priced between $1 and $5 and some extreme value items priced beyond $5, Five Below makes it easy to say YES! to the newest, coolest stuff across awesome Five Below worlds: Candy, Style, Party, Room, Create, Tech, Sports and New & Now. Founded in 2002 and headquartered in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, Five Below today has over 2,000 stores in 47 states.

analysis_md:
# FIVE — Five Below, Inc.
Pass-1 run, 2026-10-18, engine 5.4.0. Price $222.72 (nasdaq_quote_api), market cap $12,346,922,403.84 — in scope under $40B. All figures below are copied from dcf_numbers.json, ttm.json, financials_history.csv or fundamentals.json — none are recomputed.

## What it is
Specialty discount retailer running a treasure-hunt format aimed at tweens, teens and their parents ("the Kid and the Kid in all of us"): most items at $5 or less, plus a "Five Beyond" tier above $5. Ended fiscal 2026 (Jan 31, 2026) with 1,921 stores in 46 states after 150 net openings; 2,022 stores by Q2 fiscal 2027. Under CEO Winnie Park (in place since late 2024) the company executed a customer-centric reset — trend-right curated assortments, better in-stock, a peak-hours store labor model — and comps inflected from the fiscal 2024–25 trough to +12.8% in fiscal 2026 and +18.3% in H1 fiscal 2027, five straight double-digit comp quarters.

## Owner's earnings
**FY2026 (10-K, year ended 2026-01-31, from financials_history.csv):** revenue $4,764,147,000 (+22.9% YoY), operating cash flow $586,428,000, capex $174,741,000, SBC $34,680,000 (always a real cost), net income $358,641,000, D&A $192,123,000.
- **Conservative owner's earnings FY2026: $377,007,000 = $6.8006/share** (OCF − capex − SBC, on 55,436,972 diluted shares).
- Maintenance version (NI + D&A − min(capex, D&A) − ΔNWC): $400,212,000 total — same ballpark, which supports the conservative figure.
- OE positive 5 of the last 5 fiscal years, but the path is a round trip: OE/share $0.2479 (FY2022), $0.7066 (FY2023), $2.6376 (FY2024), $1.6510 (FY2025), $6.8006 (FY2026).
- Balance sheet (FY2026, financials_history.csv): cash filed only as the combined cash + restricted-cash total, $723,699,000; **no funded debt** — no current or long-term debt balances filed; equity $2,193,290,000; total assets $4,937,019,000; the real fixed obligations are operating lease liabilities of $2,032,189,000.

**TTM through Q2 fiscal 2027 (ttm.py, filing-direct, period ended 2026-08-01):**
- OCF: FY $586,428,000 − prior YTD $225,658,000 + current YTD $442,710,000 = **TTM $803,480,000**
- Capex: FY $174,741,000 − prior YTD $80,928,000 + current YTD $110,417,000 = **TTM $204,230,000**
- SBC: FY $34,680,000 − prior YTD $18,419,000 + current YTD $15,029,000 = **TTM $31,290,000**
- Shares (current-YTD weighted diluted): **55,540,532**
- **TTM OE total $567,960,000 → $10.2260/share** — computed, quoted, and **rejected as the base**: Q2 fiscal 2027 GAAP operating income was $275.4M against adjusted operating income of $113.2M (company's Q2 release, via press coverage of the print) — a ~$162M pre-tax one-time tariff recovery sits inside TTM earnings and operating cash flow (GAAP Q2 EPS $3.99 vs adjusted $1.68). A base that capitalizes a tariff refund is not a base.

**Base used = latest fiscal year OE/share, $6.8006, via `base_override` in judgment.json** (construction and reasoning quoted there; measured impact under Thoughts). The engine's normalized base (3-yr median) is $2.6376/share — rejected: the median of the last three years is literally the FY2024 print, the pre-turnaround trough (ROIC low of 16.4%, peak capex on 227 store openings), averaged against the tariff-hit FY2025. The pinned FY2026 base is post-reset and pre-refund, and it is conservative against the forward run-rate: fiscal 2027 guidance (raised after Q2) is sales $5.63–5.71B, comps +10–12%, adjusted EPS $9.83–10.31, ~150 net new stores.

## Moat: 5/10 — moderate/narrow
Justification: a differentiated treasure-hunt value format with real brand resonance for its kid/tween niche, 2,022 stores and proven new-store economics — but no switching costs, a copyable trend-driven assortment, heavyweight competition, and imported-merchandise tariff exposure. Evidence first: return on invested capital (fundamentals.json `roic_proxy`: after-tax operating income over equity + debt − cash) ran 28.1% / 29.3% / 40.2% / 30.8% / 20.3% / 27.4% / 25.2% / 20.6% / 16.4% / 23.2% across FY2017–FY2026 — well above the cost of capital in every year including the trough — and gross margin held in a 34.9–36.5% band for the decade (FY2021 dip 33.2% aside). Caveat: the proxy excludes lease liabilities from invested capital, so it flatters the level; the durability through a margin trough is the part that is real. That evidence supports a genuine but narrow moat (5), not a 7+: returns are earned on merchandising execution that must be re-won each season, and comps round-tripped from negative to +18% within three years.
- FOR: differentiated treasure-hunt format and brand aimed at tweens/teens — customers come for discovery, not staples; decade of ROIC well above the cost of capital with gross margin stable at ~35–36%; scale and new-store machine (2,022 stores, ~150 net openings/yr, 8.5% unit growth in FY2026); traffic-led comps — five straight double-digit comp quarters (Q2 FY2027 +14.1% on +13.6% transactions).
- AGAINST: no switching costs, copyable assortment; competition for the same discretionary dollar (Dollar Tree/Dollar General, Walmart, Target, TJX, Amazon, Temu/Shein); tariff exposure on imported merchandise — tariff costs depressed FY2025 earnings and the Q2 FY2027 refund one-off shows the exposure cuts both ways; comp volatility (negative in the trough, +18.3% at the peak); "Five Beyond" price creep risks diluting the value promise.
- A 5 gives CAP = 8.5 years: growth holds 2 years, then converges linearly to the 2.5% terminal rate over 8.5 years, 15-year projection.

## DCF — final run (2026-10-18)
Growth sanity check (mandatory): the engine's blended start is 21.33%, but one blend component — OE/share CAGR 2y of 60.83% — is a trough-to-peak artifact and means nothing. The revenue signals: 5-yr CAGR 19.40%, 3-yr CAGR 15.65%, latest FY +22.90%, H1 fiscal 2027 sales +27.5%. Scenario starts were set to 8 / 13 / **19** / 24 / 30% (offsets −0.1333 / −0.0833 / −0.0233 / +0.0267 / +0.0867 vs the blend). The base start (19%) sits **below** the latest FY print (+22.90%) and the H1 print (+27.5%) — written reason: management's own raised guidance implies H2 deceleration (full-year comps guided +10–12% after H1 comps of +18.3%; full-year sales guided +18.2% to +19.9%), and a DCF start is an OE growth rate held for two years, not one guided year; against that, guided adjusted EPS growth of roughly +47–55% for fiscal 2027 (adj. ## Flags — every fragility flag resolved
- **STALE_FY** (FY ended 8.5 months ago): TTM was computed with ttm.py through 2026-08-01 and is quoted in full above. It was rejected as the base because it capitalizes the Q2 tariff recovery; the FY2026 pin is used instead and the post-FY evidence (H1 sales +27.5%, comps +18.3%, guidance raised twice) is carried in the scenario starts.
- **BASE_DIVERGENCE** (latest FY $6.80 vs 3-yr median $2.64): **both** are distorted, in opposite directions — the median is the FY2024 trough print (pre-turnaround, peak capex), the latest year is flattered by trough capex, and the TTM ($10.2260) is flattered by the tariff refund. Resolution: pin the latest FY ($6.8006) as the least-distorted audited year and charge capex normalization to the bear multipliers. Declared as `base_override` in judgment.json with the construction quoted from this run's own outputs.
- **OE_VOLATILE** (OE/share spans >3x over 5 years): real — it is a margin/capex round trip (trough FY2024–25, peak FY2026), not steady cyclicality. Handled by the clean-year base pin plus bear-side weight of 40% (15% super bear + 25% bear).
- **NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE** (fiscal 2025, year ended 2025-02-01: net income $253,611,000 vs OCF $430,648,000): the $177.0M gap is ~95% the non-cash D&A addback (D&A $167,447,000 that year, financials_history.csv); the residual is ordinary working capital. No tax-deposit, impairment or other one-off was found — and the base is built from OCF, so the divergence does not contaminate it.
- **DEBT_TAGS_BLANK** (no debt tag for the latest fiscal year): stated from the filing balance sheet — Five Below carries **no funded debt**: no current or long-term debt balances are filed for FY2026; the company is financed by equity of $2,193,290,000 and operating leases. Net debt is null because there is no debt to net, not because data is missing. The leverage that exists is lease leverage: operating lease liabilities $2,032,189,000.
- **CASH_INCLUDES_RESTRICTED** (only the combined cash + restricted tag is filed, $723,699,000 at FY2026 end): with zero funded debt there is no net-debt figure for the restricted slice to understate; the combined cash total matters only as a partial offset to the $2,032,189,000 of lease liabilities, which are obligations regardless of the split. No verdict in this analysis rests on the cash split.
- **WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD** (super-bull IV 4.05x super-bear IV): real — turnaround durability plus tariff exposure make the outcome range genuinely wide. Confidence is capped at medium and the verdict is sized to the conservative end.
- **TIER_BAND** (bear tier D at 7.19% vs bull tier C at 11.31%): the verdict is sized to the bear end — Tier D.
- (Preliminary-run **LOW_OE_YIELD** at 1.2% was an artifact of the trough median base; on the pinned base the OE yield is 3.05% — still thin, which is why the verdict does not bend toward the bull case.)

## My thoughts / overlay
- The honest headline is the **method range**, and for once it is one-directional: on the engine's median base with default scenarios (preliminary run) weighted IRR was 5.81% with IV@15% $49.88 (Tier D); on the pinned latest-FY base, 9.28% / $110.97 (Tier D); on the raw TTM base with identical scenarios, 12.23% / $166.86 (Tier C). Every defensible base — including one that capitalizes a one-time tariff refund — leaves the stock short of the 15% hurdle at $222.72. The market has already paid for the turnaround; what remains is execution risk the buyer is not compensated for.
- **Override impact (measured, from the runs above):** the base_override moves the base from the engine-native $2.6376 to $6.8006 (+157.8%) and the weighted IRR from 5.81% (preliminary default-scenario run) to 9.28% on the final scenario set — large, and it still does not change the tier. Without the override the name would print a trough-company verdict; with it, a fairly-priced-recovery verdict. Tier D either way.
- Quality is not the debate: a debt-free balance sheet (leases aside), a decade of ROIC above the cost of capital, gross margin that never broke, SBC a modest $34.7M (5.9% of OCF in FY2026), buybacks resumed (Q2 fiscal 2027: ~311,000 shares for ~$60.0M per the Q2 release), share count essentially flat (−0.18%/yr).
- Risks: comps are running at unsustainable levels (+18.3% H1) against the anniversary of the reset — guidance already implies a hard H2 deceleration; tariff policy is a live, two-sided exposure on an imported assortment (costs hurt FY2025, a refund flattered Q2 FY2027 — neither is run-rate); new-store returns must hold as the base passes 2,000 stores; "Five Beyond" price creep vs the value promise; a consumer downturn hits discretionary treasure-hunt spending first.
- Margin of safety: there is none at this price on owner's earnings — the weighted IV@15% is half the price, and even the super-bull IV@15% ($212.61) is below it. A buyer at $222.72 needs the super-bull path merely to approach a 15% return (super-bull IRR 14.54%).

## Final verdict
- **Final tier: D** (weighted IRR 9.28% on the pinned latest-FY base; method range D to C across the median / latest-FY / TTM bases)
- Confidence: **Medium** (high on the filing arithmetic and the balance sheet; the wide scenario spread and the unproven durability of the comp surge cap it there)
- One-liner: Turnaround value retailer, moat 5/10 with a decade of high ROIC — but at $222.72 the market already pays for the recovery: weighted IRR 9.3% (IV@15% $110.97) on the clean latest-FY base, and even the tariff-refund-inflated TTM base reaches only 12.2%; clears the 15% hurdle only below ~$111.
